CHIEF COMPLAINT
Shortness of breath

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Rachel is a 48-year-old female presenting with shortness of breath. She reports experiencing shortness of breath with mild exercise or even walking (such as walking up her driveway), accompanied by palpitations. She is uncertain whether these symptoms are related to her chronic back pain. She notes that the symptoms have been occurring more frequently lately. Patient has recently increased her exercise regimen to lose weight. She reports a significant reduction in smoking, from 2 packs per day to approximately 1 cigarette per day. Pulmonary function tests were obtained and suggest possible asthma or COPD. Chest x-ray demonstrates a flattened diaphragm consistent with COPD findings. Physical examination reveals mild wheezes in all lung fields.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies other concerning issues.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression
Chronic back pain
Smoking history

MEDICATIONS
Effexor (for depression)
Gabapentin/Neurontin (for chronic back pain)

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Smoking: Previously 2 packs per day, currently reduced to approximately 1 cigarette per day
Exercise: Recently increased to lose weight
Yoga: Considered but not regularly practiced

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Appears well
Lungs: Mild wheezes in all lung fields
Otherwise normal examination

RESULTS
Pulmonary function tests: Consistent with possible asthma or COPD
Chest x-ray: Flattened diaphragm, findings consistent with COPD

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
COPD (Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease). Patient initiated on Combivent 2 puffs twice daily to help open lungs. Albuterol prescribed 2 puffs as needed for shortness of breath rescue. Prednisone taper pack prescribed. Continue Effexor for depression without changes. Continue Neurontin for chronic back pain without changes. Encouraged to practice yoga for depression and back pain management.
